A.explanation: Current is an SI base quantity, but its SI base unit is the ampere, symbol $A$, not current.

B.explanation: The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram, symbol $\text{kg}$, not the gram.

C.explanation: The kelvin, symbol $K$, is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.

D.explanation: The volt is a derived unit for potential difference, equal to $\text{J C}^{-1}$, not a base unit.

hints: Notice the question asks for a base unit, not a base quantity - so check whether each word names a quantity or a unit.
Recall the seven SI base units: kilogram, metre, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela, and what quantities they measure.
Compare gram with kilogram for mass, and ask whether volt can be built from other units such as joule and coulomb.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: one of the four names must be exactly an SI base unit, with correct name and status.

Recall the SI base quantities and units: length in metre, mass in kilogram, time in second, electric current in ampere, thermodynamic temperature in kelvin, amount of substance in mole, luminous intensity in candela.
Check option A: electric current is a base quantity, but the unit is the ampere, so the word current is not a unit.
Check option B: mass is a base quantity, but its base unit is the kilogram, so gram is only a fraction $10^{-3} \text{ kg}$ and not the base unit.
Check option D: volt measures potential difference and can be expressed as $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-3} \text{A}^{-1}$, so it is a derived unit.
The remaining name, kelvin, is the defined base unit for temperature and cannot be broken into other units. This is option C.
